question: Why would a nurse place the bell of a stethoscope over an enlarged thyroid gland?

options.A: To listen for a bruit caused by increased blood flow
options.B: To check for crackles moving up from the trachea
options.C: To measure the exact width of the thyroid lobes
options.D: To assess for abnormal whistling breath sounds

explanation: An overactive thyroid sucks up a massive amount of blood. That rushing blood creates an audible whooshing sound called a bruit that you can actually hear through your stethoscope!

question: Why do public health teams collect blood or stool samples during a suspected outbreak?

options.A: To test the quality of local drinking water pipes only
options.B: To measure the general nutritional status of healthy adults
options.C: To calculate the daily operational costs of the clinic
options.D: To identify the specific causative agent in a laboratory

explanation: Lab tests on these samples tell us the exact germ, bacteria, or virus causing the trouble, helping us choose the exact right treatment.

question: Which type of drug reaction specifically needs the patient to have been exposed to the drug before?

options.A: Allergic reaction
options.B: Idiosyncratic reaction
options.C: Toxic overdose reaction
options.D: Cumulative drug effect

explanation: An allergy usually requires a first exposure to sensitize the body, so the immune system can react fiercely the next time. Keep building that knowledge!

question: What is the main goal of taking anti-seizure medications?

options.A: To prevent future seizures by stabilizing brain activity
options.B: To permanently cure the underlying cause of epilepsy
options.C: To increase the speed of brain electrical signals
options.D: To immediately stop pain during a headache

explanation: These meds act like a steady anchor for the brain, calming down hyperactive nerve cells so seizures don't catch the patient off guard. You've got this concept down!

question: Which of these is NOT an expected result of taking a sympathomimetic drug?

options.A: Pupil dilation
options.B: Bronchodilation
options.C: Increased heart rate
options.D: Decreased heart rate

explanation: Sympathomimetic drugs mimic the sympathetic system—they speed things up, open airways, and widen pupils. They won't slow down the heart rate!

question: Why do nurses need to care about the food myths our patients believe?

options.A: Myths directly shape daily eating habits and health choices
options.B: Nurses are required to rewrite local recipe books
options.C: Patients will refuse all medications if they have food myths
options.D: Myths are always illegal to follow in a hospital setting

explanation: What people believe dictates what they put on their plates. Understanding this helps us guide patients better without making them feel judged!

question: What is the main danger of the clotting-heavy state (hypercoagulability) seen in pregnancy?

options.A: Sudden and severe drop in total white blood cell count
options.B: Permanent destruction of all circulating platelets
options.C: Inability of the blood to form any scabs after a cut
options.D: Increased risk of unwanted blood clots in the veins

explanation: The body gets ready to prevent heavy bleeding after birth, but this downside means blood can form dangerous clots in the legs too easily.

question: What is the main goal of doing a mental status examination during a home visit?

options.A: To measure the client's physical strength and reflexes
options.B: To test the client's long-term memory from childhood
options.C: To evaluate the current cognitive and psychological functioning of the client
options.D: To diagnose the exact subtype of personality disorder

explanation: You got it! The mental status exam gives us a quick, structured snapshot of how the patient is thinking and behaving right now.

question: Which specific area of the body does a colonoscopy examine?

options.A: The large intestine and rectum
options.B: The upper esophagus and stomach
options.C: The trachea and lower bronchial tubes
options.D: The urinary bladder and urethra

explanation: A colonoscopy is specifically designed to inspect the lining of the large bowel and the rectum. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T2#GNS221_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which set of clinical signs points directly to neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS)?

options.A: High fever, extreme muscle rigidity, and unstable vitals
options.B: Uncontrolled euphoria and excessive talkativeness
options.C: Hyperactive bowel sounds and sudden weight loss
options.D: Slurred speech, itchy skin rash, and low fever

explanation: Think of NMS as a dangerous fire in the body: extremely high fever, muscles stiff as boards (lead-pipe rigidity), and wild swings in blood pressure and heart rate.

question: When is a syringe driver most likely to be used for a patient?

options.A: When the patient refuses all forms of nursing care
options.B: When intravenous access is completely forbidden by law
options.C: When the patient needs rapid blood pressure support
options.D: When oral medications are no longer safe or possible

explanation: Exactly! If a patient cannot swallow, has severe vomiting, or is nearing the end of life, a syringe driver is a lifesaver for giving regular medications smoothly.

question: What is the dark vertical line that often appears on a pregnant belly called?

options.A: Linea nigra
options.B: Striae gravidarum
options.C: Melasma gravidarum
options.D: Vascular spider

explanation: Great job! Linea nigra simply means 'black line' in Latin—it's that common dark stripe that shows up on the tummy due to extra skin pigment.

question: What is the most common reason people develop Wernicke encephalopathy?

options.A: A sudden head injury
options.B: A bad food allergy
options.C: Eating too much sugar
options.D: Chronic alcohol misuse

explanation: Correct! Long-term heavy alcohol use stops the gut from absorbing thiamine properly, making it the top cause of this condition.

question: Why can forcing large meals cause problems for a patient with an advanced illness?

options.A: It causes physical distress like nausea and cramping
options.B: It instantly cures the loss of appetite
options.C: It interferes with daily physical therapy
options.D: It speeds up the metabolism too quickly

explanation: Spot on! When the body is weak, its digestive system slows down. Heavy meals just lead to discomfort like belly pain and nausea, rather than good nutrition.

question: What is the medical term for having an abnormally low platelet count, which increases a patient's risk of bleeding?

options.A: Anemia
options.B: Polycythemia
options.C: Thrombocytopenia
options.D: Leukemia

explanation: Well done! 'Thrombo' relates to clotting, 'cyto' to cells, and 'penia' means deficiency. Put it together, and thrombocytopenia means low platelets and bleeding risk.

question: Why is the initial binding between sperm and egg membrane proteins so important?

options.A: It immediately triggers the shedding of all female chromosomes
options.B: It stops the sperm from releasing any digestive enzymes
options.C: It ensures species-specific recognition before the cell membranes can fuse
options.D: It permanently seals the uterus against outside infections

explanation: The proteins act like a security check, making sure human sperm matches with a human egg before letting cell fusion happen.

question: What does a sudden, rapid change in a patient's weight usually point to in clinical practice?

options.A: Permanent alterations in height
options.B: Immediate changes in bone density
options.C: Fluctuations in body fluid balance
options.D: Rapid muscle tissue hypertrophy

explanation: When weight shifts overnight, it's almost always water gain or loss rather than actual tissue changes. Good thing to keep in mind on the ward!

question: What vital equipment must always be kept ready at the bedside of a patient recovering from an airway issue?

options.A: A standard blood pressure cuff and stethoscope
options.B: Suction machine and a manual breathing bag
options.C: A sterile surgical tray for major tummy surgery
options.D: An intravenous infusion pump with extra tubing

explanation: Always be prepared! Having suction and a bag-valve-mask right at the bedside lets nurses act instantly if thick mucus blocks the airway or breathing slows down.

question: A patient reports severe burning and pain immediately after receiving ear drops. What is the nurse's first action?

options.A: Wait ten minutes to see if the pain goes away on its own
options.B: Stop the procedure and report the reaction to the doctor
options.C: Pack the ear canal tightly with sterile gauze
options.D: Reassure the patient and give a second dose right away

explanation: Severe pain means something is wrong, so the nurse must stop immediately and seek medical guidance. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h8)

question: Why should we avoid giving strong painkillers before a doctor figures out the exact cause of a severe tummy ache?

options.A: It stops the kidneys from making urine
options.B: It immediately drops the patient's blood pressure
options.C: It always damages the stomach lining
options.D: It can hide warning signs of a surgical emergency like a burst organ

explanation: Pain is actually a helpful clue! If painkillers wipe it out completely, doctors might miss critical signs that a patient urgently needs surgery.

question: How does long-term release of cortisol help the body cope with extended stress?

options.A: By increasing available blood glucose and energy supplies
options.B: By lowering the heart rate and blood pressure to rest
options.C: By promoting rapid storage of extra body fat in muscles
options.D: By enhancing digestion and nutrient absorption in the gut

explanation: Cortisol breaks down stored fats and proteins to keep your blood sugar up, ensuring your body has plenty of energy to push through tough, stressful times.

question: Which of these is an example of an internal factor that can affect a person's health?

options.A: Cultural family traditions
options.B: Availability of community hospitals
options.C: Genetic makeup and inherited traits
options.D: Socioeconomic income level

explanation: You've got this! Internal factors come from within us—like our genes, age, and sex—while external factors come from our surroundings.

question: Which of the following is considered a consumable medical supply?

options.A: An overhead patient bed
options.B: A mercury sphygmomanometer
options.C: A hospital wheelchair
options.D: Disposable syringes

explanation: Consumables are single-use items that get thrown away after one application, like syringes and gauze. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h2)

question: What do high-pressure alarms usually tell you about a mechanically ventilated patient?

options.A: The patient is breathing too slowly or not at all
options.B: Changes in lung compliance or increased airway resistance
options.C: A disconnection of the main tubing from the patient
options.D: A power failure in the wall electrical socket

explanation: When the high-pressure alarm sounds, it means something is making it harder to push air in—like mucus plugs, coughing, or the patient biting the tube. Time to put on your detective hat and check the patient!

question: What is the main difference between infiltration and extravasation?

options.A: Extravasation makes the skin feel very cold, whereas infiltration makes it feel hot
options.B: Infiltration only happens in the legs, while extravasation happens in the arms
options.C: Extravasation involves tissue-damaging vesicant drugs that can cause necrosis
options.D: Infiltration requires immediate surgical removal of the vein tissue

explanation: Both mean fluid leaked out of the vein, but extravasation is extra scary because the leaked drug is a 'vesicant' that can actually destroy the surrounding tissue and cause severe sores.

question: Which ethical principle is all about actively doing good and helping your patient?

options.A: Beneficence
options.B: Autonomy
options.C: Veracity
options.D: Justice

explanation: Think of Beneficence as your active duty to do good and boost the health and well-being of everyone in your care. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h2)

question: What is the term when a brain injury causes a client to completely ignore one entire side of their body or room?

options.A: Apraxia
options.B: Unilateral neglect
options.C: Global amnesia
options.D: Expressive aphasia

explanation: Unilateral neglect can feel baffling to the client—their brain literally forgets that one side of the world (or their own body) exists. As nurses, we help bridge that gap!

question: Which physical exam technique involves tapping on the body to check what is underneath?

options.A: Palpation
options.B: Percussion
options.C: Inspection
options.D: Auscultation

explanation: Spot on! Percussion is like playing a small drum on the skin. The sound tells you if the organ underneath is full of air, fluid, or solid.

question: Which type of hospital structure features a long, top-down chain of command with many layers of management?

options.A: Bureaucratic structure
options.B: Matrix structure
options.C: Flat structure
options.D: Informal structure

explanation: Think of a bureaucratic structure like a tall ladder. Decisions and orders have to climb up and down many distinct steps of management.

question: A mother asks what food to first give her six-month-old. What is the best nurse response?

options.A: Cow milk straight from the carton to build strong bones
options.B: Clear vegetable broths with added table salt for taste
options.C: Sweetened fruit juices to encourage quick swallowing
options.D: Thick, nutrient-dense mashed foods like iron-fortified porridge or yam

explanation: First foods should be thick and rich in nutrients, especially iron, to match the rapid growth spurt of a six-month-old baby.

question: What is the best way to handle a client who expresses fear that an injectable contraceptive causes permanent barrenness?

options.A: Refuse to provide any family planning services to uneducated clients
options.B: Laugh at the misconception so they realize how silly it sounds
options.C: Tell them they must accept whatever side effects happen without complaining
options.D: Listen patiently, validate their worry, and provide factual reassurance

explanation: Respectful dialogue and clear facts help dispel deep-seated cultural myths without shaming the client. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h7)

question: What is the main job of prostaglandins when childbirth is about to start?

options.A: softening the cervix and stimulating uterine contractions
options.B: blocking maternal pain receptors in the spinal cord
options.C: maintaining high blood pressure to perfuse the placenta
options.D: suppressing the release of fetal cortisol from the adrenal glands

explanation: Well done! Prostaglandins act locally to soften and ripen the cervix so the uterus can start contracting effectively.

question: What should the nurse check when inspecting the dressing after the procedure?

options.A: Whether the skin has turned a pale yellow color
options.B: If the adhesive tape is completely waterproof
options.C: Signs of bleeding, swelling, or fluid leakage
options.D: The exact temperature of the bandage material

explanation: Spot on! Regular site checks ensure any bleeding or fluid leakage is caught and managed early.

question: Why is it important to ask a patient about their current medications during a neuro history?

options.A: Medications completely cure all neurological disorders
options.B: Many drugs can alter mental status or cause tremors
options.C: Pharmaceutical records replace physical examinations
options.D: Drugs are the only cause of sudden vision loss

explanation: Certain drugs and everyday meds can make a patient feel confused or cause shaky hands, which can easily look like a brain problem if you don't check their drug history.

question: What does milking a drainage tube involve?

options.A: Disconnecting the drainage bag completely and washing the inside with soap
options.B: Injecting large volumes of sterile water upward into the wound site
options.C: Twisting the tube tightly until the fluid stops flowing completely
options.D: Gently squeezing and releasing the tubing downward to push clots along

explanation: Milking is a gentle technique used to clear minor blockages by compressing the tubing progressively toward the collection container. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at a primary health clinic presents with facial swelling, blurred vision, and a blood pressure of 160/110 mmHg. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Give her paracetamol tablets and ask her to wait
options.B: Advise her to drink plenty of palm wine and sleep
options.C: Send her home with instructions to rest for a week
options.D: Refer her urgently to a secondary or tertiary facility

explanation: These are signs of severe pre-eclampsia, which can quickly lead to deadly eclamptic seizures if not managed in a hospital. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h4)

question: How does COVID-19 mostly spread from person to person?

options.A: By drinking contaminated municipal water supplies
options.B: Through the bite of infected mosquitoes and ticks
options.C: By consuming undercooked poultry and beef products
options.D: Through respiratory droplets from coughing and talking

explanation: You got it! Tiny droplets released into the air when people talk, cough, or sneeze are the main way the virus travels. Simple infection control basics!

question: What CD4 count marks the official shift from HIV to AIDS?

options.A: Below 1,000 cells/mm³
options.B: Below 500 cells/mm³
options.C: Below 200 cells/mm³
options.D: Below 800 cells/mm³

explanation: You got it! When the immune system's CD4 count drops below 200 cells/mm³, the diagnosis is classified as AIDS. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T2#GNS216_U6_T2_h6)

question: Why do doctors still check cervical polyps even though they are usually harmless?

options.A: To stop chronic pelvic pain
options.B: To prevent permanent infertility
options.C: To rule out potential malignancy
options.D: To cure underlying bacterial infections

explanation: Even though most polyps are completely harmless, doctors always check them just to be 100% sure there are no hidden cancer cells. Better safe than sorry!

question: What color zone on a Shakir MUAC tape indicates severe acute malnutrition?

options.A: Green
options.B: Yellow
options.C: Red
options.D: Blue

explanation: The red zone warns of severe malnutrition, signaling that the child needs urgent medical and nutritional rescue. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h5)

question: Which device is commonly managed by modern critical care nurses to support kidney function?

options.A: Automated external pacemaker for heart block
options.B: Negative-pressure iron lung for breathing
options.C: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) machine
options.D: Intra-aortic balloon pump for cardiac support

explanation: CRRT is a specialized form of dialysis used in the ICU for critically ill patients with acute kidney injury. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h6)

question: A nurse needs to draw medication from a multidose vial for another patient. Which of these actions is unsafe?

options.A: Swabbing the rubber top of the vial with an alcohol wipe before piercing
options.B: Using a brand new, sterile syringe and needle for drawing up the dose
options.C: Checking the expiration date printed on the label of the vial
options.D: Leaving a previously used dispensing needle inserted in the vial rubber septum

explanation: Never leave a needle stuck inside a multidose vial! It acts like an open door for bacteria to crawl inside and contaminate the medicine for the next patient.

question: What is the key trait of a polyvalent nurse?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on surgical nursing care
options.B: Training across multiple clinical specialties
options.C: Specializing in pediatric medicine only
options.D: Working only in hospital management roles

explanation: Spot on! A polyvalent nurse is cross-trained in different fields, meaning they can comfortably move and work across various hospital departments.

question: What is the main perk of doing a 24-hour urine collection instead of just one blood test?

options.A: It captures total hormone output and smooths out hourly spikes
options.B: It measures intracellular hormone synthesis inside the bone marrow
options.C: It requires no special patient preparation or storage rules
options.D: It can be completed in less than five minutes at the bedside

explanation: Hormones can spike and dip all day long. Collecting urine over a full 24 hours gives a complete, average picture of what the body is putting out!

question: What nursing action should be performed immediately after removing the flatus tube?

options.A: Check the patient's blood pressure
options.B: Insert a new tube into the urethra
options.C: Clean and dry the perianal area
options.D: Administer a strong oral laxative

explanation: Cleaning the perianal area removes any residual lubricant or discharge, ensuring skin integrity and patient comfort. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h5)

question: Why do nurses often recommend simple activities like brisk walking instead of expensive gyms?

options.A: Gyms are strictly illegal in most rural Nigerian communities
options.B: Walking burns zero calories compared to gym equipment
options.C: Outdoor exercise is the only way to build muscle strength
options.D: It encourages long-term adherence by fitting into everyday life

explanation: You got it! Affordable and practical activities are much easier for people to keep doing consistently over time without getting stressed.

question: Why is dragging a patient straight across bedsheets a bad idea for their skin?

options.A: It completely blocks the production of natural skin oils
options.B: It forces moisture deep into the subcutaneous fat layer
options.C: It creates friction and shear forces that damage skin and blood vessels
options.D: It causes an immediate drop in the patient's systemic blood pressure

explanation: Correct! Pulling someone across rough sheets creates friction and tears tiny blood vessels underneath. Always lift, never drag!

question: What is the very first thing emergency responders do at an accident scene to protect a patient's spine?

options.A: Administering strong intravenous pain medication
options.B: Standing the patient up to test leg strength
options.C: Applying a rigid neck collar and securing the body
options.D: Massaging the neck muscles to relieve tension

explanation: That's correct! Putting on a stiff neck collar and securing the body keeps the spine still, preventing small fractures from turning into permanent paralysis.

question: What key instruction should you give a patient about how much topical cream to use?

options.A: Mix all prescribed creams together to save time
options.B: Use only the exact prescribed amount in a thin layer
options.C: Stop applying the cream the moment the redness fades slightly
options.D: Apply as much as possible so it cures the condition faster

explanation: More isn't always better! Piling on extra cream doesn't speed up healing; it just increases the risk of skin irritation and unwanted side effects.

question: What is the main goal of medical asepsis in the ward?

options.A: To kill all bacterial spores
options.B: To replace hand hygiene completely
options.C: To sterilize all medical instruments
options.D: To reduce the number of germs

explanation: Medical asepsis is all about cutting down the number of germs and stopping them from spreading. Surgical asepsis, on the other hand, aims for complete sterility. You're doing great!

question: Which body part is mainly affected in a Type I FGM procedure?

options.A: The perineal body
options.B: The vaginal opening
options.C: The clitoris
options.D: The entire labia majora

explanation: Type I FGM specifically involves removing all or part of the clitoris or its surrounding hood (prepuce).

question: Which infection control step is absolutely mandatory when nursing a suspected Lassa fever patient?

options.A: Placing every patient in a carpeted, air-conditioned room
options.B: Allowing family members to wash the patient's soiled linens
options.C: Using full personal protective equipment and barrier nursing
options.D: Administering prophylactic antibiotics to all hospital visitors

explanation: Barrier nursing with full PPE is non-negotiable to keep infectious body fluids away from staff and other patients.

question: What is the main goal of a safe injection according to the WHO?

options.A: To completely eliminate the use of oral medications in the hospital
options.B: To prevent harm to the patient and worker without creating dangerous waste
options.C: To ensure medications are absorbed twice as fast into the bloodstream
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing disposable syringes

explanation: A safe injection protects everyone: the patient getting the drug, you as the nurse giving it, and the community from bad waste disposal. You've got this!

question: Where do the nerve fibers in the dorsal column pathway cross over to the opposite side of the body?

options.A: The lumbar spinal cord
options.B: The peripheral skin receptor
options.C: The medulla oblongata
options.D: The cerebral cortex

explanation: Spot on! As these sensory messages travel up, they cross over to the other side once they reach the lower part of the brainstem called the medulla.

question: Which medication group is most commonly given via nebulizer to relax tightened airway muscles?

options.A: Vasopressors
options.B: Anticoagulants
options.C: Antibiotics
options.D: Bronchodilators

explanation: Bronchodilators open up constricted breathing tubes so air can flow freely in and out of the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of a performance appraisal in nursing management?

options.A: To find reasons to terminate employee contracts immediately
options.B: To replace daily clinical supervision entirely
options.C: To evaluate job performance and guide professional growth
options.D: To decide which nurse gets the biggest office space

explanation: Appraisals measure work against standards to help staff improve their clinical practice and develop professionally. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h6)

question: Why must a nurse evaluate both the urinary and reproductive systems together?

options.A: Patients cannot distinguish between urinary and reproductive pain
options.B: Issues in one system often directly affect the other
options.C: The anatomical structures share the exact same nerve supply
options.D: Hospital policies mandate performing both exams simultaneously

explanation: Because the urinary and reproductive systems share close anatomical proximity and pathways, pathology in one frequently impacts the other. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T2#GNS213_U4_T2_h1)

question: What is a common long-term problem after severe injury and healing of the voice box (larynx)?

options.A: Loss of the sense of smell and taste
options.B: Spontaneous closure of the food pipe
options.C: Airway narrowing (stenosis) from scar tissue
options.D: Permanent widening of the windpipe

explanation: You got it! As damaged tissues heal, extra scar formation can contract and narrow the airway passage, causing breathing trouble later.

question: Which of these is a good example of objective documentation during a reproductive assessment?

options.A: Patient seems overly anxious and does not like pelvic exams
options.B: Skin intact, no lesions or abnormal discharge noted on the labia
options.C: Patient is probably hiding symptoms due to personal embarrassment
options.D: External genitalia look completely normal and healthy overall

explanation: Spot on! Objective notes focus on clear, observable facts rather than personal guesses or vague opinions.

question: What is the purpose of the clean apron inside the home visiting kit?

options.A: To protect the nurse's uniform from contamination
options.B: To dry the patient's hands after washing
options.C: To serve as a clean bandage for large wounds
options.D: To keep the nurse warm in cold weather

explanation: The apron acts as a barrier between the nurse's clothes and the patient's immediate surroundings during care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h2)

question: You notice your clinic frequently runs out of single-use syringes, causing staff to reuse equipment. What is your best professional action?

options.A: Keep quiet so you don't upset the clinic manager during a busy shift
options.B: Buy plastic syringes from a local pharmacy using your own money
options.C: Stop giving all prescribed medications until the hospital closes
options.D: Report the shortage through official channels and advocate for safer supplies

explanation: Spot on! As a nurse, you have a duty to advocate for your patients and push for proper resources when safety is on the line. Great clinical leadership! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h9)

question: A community nurse notices a sudden weekly jump in new diarrhea cases in a local village. What should be done first?

options.A: Assume the data collection error is harmless and ignore it
options.B: Wait until the end of the year to calculate annual prevalence
options.C: Close all local schools permanently without further testing
options.D: Investigate possible sources like contaminated water supplies

explanation: Brilliant clinical thinking! A sudden spike means you need to hunt down the source—like bad drinking water—right away to stop the spread.

question: What is the main difference between a hypertensive urgency and a hypertensive emergency?

options.A: The patient's age and previous history of cardiac disease
options.B: The presence of acute target organ damage in emergencies
options.C: The absolute numerical reading of the diastolic blood pressure
options.D: The requirement for oral medication in emergency settings

explanation: You got it! An emergency means high blood pressure is actively damaging vital organs (like the brain or heart), whereas an urgency has high readings without active organ harm.

question: What is meant by 'intra-household food distribution'?

options.A: How international organizations ship relief food to disaster zones.
options.B: How supermarkets transport goods from warehouses to neighborhood stores.
options.C: How the government distributes farming subsidies to rural communities.
options.D: How food is shared and divided among people living in the same home.

explanation: Spot on! This simply looks at who gets what share of the pot right inside your own house.

question: Which laboratory test is used to definitively diagnose sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.B: Coagulation profile test
options.C: Complete blood count
options.D: Haemoglobin electrophoresis

explanation: Haemoglobin electrophoresis is the gold standard test! It separates different types of haemoglobin in a sample so the lab can clearly spot abnormal haemoglobin S.

question: Why is it so important to translate health messages into local indigenous languages?

options.A: It ensures clear comprehension and reduces cultural barriers
options.B: It is a legal requirement for opening a private clinic
options.C: It eliminates the need for any visual educational posters
options.D: It prevents young people from learning foreign languages

explanation: Correct! Using local languages ensures everyone understands the message clearly, making healthcare respectful and truly accessible.

question: What type of feedback loop is most often used to keep hormone levels balanced?

options.A: Positive feedback
options.B: Negative feedback
options.C: Cyclic feedback
options.D: Neutral feedback

explanation: You nailed it! Negative feedback acts like a thermostat, turning hormone production up or down to keep things stable.

question: You are caring for a patient with long-standing diabetes. Which assessment is key for tertiary prevention of microvascular issues?

options.A: Measuring handgrip strength using a dynamometer
options.B: Palpating superficial lymph nodes in the neck
options.C: Asking about daily recreational screen time habits
options.D: Checking urine for microalbumin and performing foot exams

explanation: Spot on! Checking urine for tiny amounts of protein (microalbumin) and inspecting the feet regularly helps catch early kidney and nerve damage.

question: Which term describes a dispute happening between the Emergency Department and the Surgical Ward?

options.A: Intergroup conflict
options.B: Intragroup conflict
options.C: Intrapersonal conflict
options.D: Internalized conflict

explanation: When two separate teams or departments lock horns, it's called intergroup conflict. 'Inter' means between different groups!

question: Which bed position is best for instantly helping an out-of-breath patient expand their lungs?

options.A: Trendelenburg position
options.B: High-Fowler's position
options.C: Prone lying position
options.D: Flat supine position

explanation: Sitting upright in High-Fowler's position uses gravity to push abdominal organs downward, giving the lungs more room to fill with air. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which tool is best for measuring the standing height of an adult patient?

options.A: Knee height calipers
options.B: An infant length board
options.C: A stadiometer
options.D: A flexible cloth sewing tape

explanation: A stadiometer is the standard tool with a vertical backboard and sliding headpiece built specifically to measure standing height accurately.

question: What does the term 'unmet need for family planning' actually mean?

options.A: Doctors refusing to prescribe medicines to married couples
options.B: The total absence of hospitals in a given region
options.C: Willingness to avoid pregnancy without using modern contraception
options.D: A complete ban on all contraceptive drugs by the government

explanation: An 'unmet need' simply describes women who want to delay or stop having children, but aren't currently using any modern birth control method—often due to lack of access or information.

question: Which layer of a blood vessel wall is primarily responsible for regulating vessel diameter and blood pressure?

options.A: Tunica media
options.B: Tunica adventitia
options.C: Tunica intima
options.D: Tunica externa

explanation: The tunica media contains smooth muscle cells that contract or relax to alter the caliber and resistance of the blood vessel. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the main reason governments place heavy taxes on tobacco and sugary drinks?

options.A: To completely ban all agricultural farming activities in rural farming communities
options.B: To fund the construction of large international airports in every state capital
options.C: To make healthcare workers richer through direct salary commission bonuses
options.D: To discourage consumption and lower the population's risk of developing NCDs

explanation: Spot on! When unhealthy items become more expensive, people tend to buy less of them, which helps lower community rates of lifestyle diseases.

question: How does hospice philosophy view the dying process?

options.A: As an unpredictable event requiring intensive surgery
options.B: As a natural part of the human life cycle
options.C: As a condition that can always be reversed with therapy
options.D: As a medical failure that must be fought at all costs

explanation: Hospice care embraces dying as a normal stage of life rather than viewing it purely as a medical failure. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h2)

question: What is the best eating strategy for an HIV patient dealing with severe nausea?

options.A: Avoiding all fluids for twelve hours
options.B: Eating three large oily meals daily
options.C: Consuming heavy, highly spiced foods
options.D: Eating small, frequent, bland meals

explanation: Correct! Small, gentle meals keep the stomach from feeling overloaded and help keep nausea at bay.

question: Why do nurses need to explain that emergency contraceptives are not abortifacients?

options.A: To show that they can also cure sexually transmitted infections
options.B: To prove that the drugs are 100 percent effective every time
options.C: To encourage patients to use them instead of regular condoms
options.D: To clear up cultural and moral misconceptions about how the drugs work

explanation: A lot of people mix up emergency pills with abortion pills. As a nurse, clarifying how it actually works helps calm unnecessary fears and clears up social myths. Brilliant work!

question: At an antenatal clinic in Nigeria, a pregnant woman receives sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine. What is this for?

options.A: Malaria
options.B: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Neural tube defects

explanation: Well done! In malaria-endemic areas like Nigeria, intermittent preventive treatment (IPTp) with SP is a routine lifesaver for pregnant mums.

question: A typhoid patient suddenly complains of severe, sharp belly pain and their tummy feels hard to the touch. What emergency does this point to?

options.A: Intestinal perforation
options.B: Renal stone formation
options.C: Pulmonary embolism
options.D: Splenic rupture

explanation: Correct! A rigid tummy and sudden sharp pain are red flags for a perforated bowel—this needs urgent surgical help right away.

question: Why do we take a thorough health history before checking a patient's eyes, ears, nose, and throat (EENT)?

options.A: To find out their exact insurance coverage
options.B: To diagnose complex systemic diseases on our own
options.C: To spot key symptoms and guide the physical exam
options.D: To replace the physical exam completely

explanation: Spotting early clues like pain or discharge helps you and the doctor know exactly where to focus during the physical check. Great job!

question: Why do families in traditional societies sometimes continue the practice of early marriage?

options.A: Because schools refuse to educate unmarried teenagers
options.B: Because local healthcare workers strongly encourage adolescent unions
options.C: Because modern laws actively mandate early marriage for population growth
options.D: Because it is deeply rooted in generational customs and community expectations

explanation: That's correct! Long-standing traditions create powerful community expectations, making families fear going against what their ancestors practiced.

question: How do mast cell stabilizers stop allergic symptoms from starting?

options.A: By directly destroying free-floating allergen particles
options.B: By permanently shrinking the size of mucous glands
options.C: By replacing natural antibodies in the bloodstream
options.D: By stopping mast cells from bursting and releasing histamine

explanation: You nailed it! They act like strong shields, keeping mast cell walls intact so the histamine inside cannot escape to cause trouble.

question: What is the most important instruction for a patient after an IVP procedure is finished?

options.A: Take a strong diuretic medication to stimulate urine flow
options.B: Avoid eating any solid foods until the following morning
options.C: Drink plenty of fluids to help flush out the contrast dye
options.D: Remain completely on bed rest for the next twenty-four hours

explanation: Water is the best helper here! Drinking plenty of fluids helps the kidneys wash the remaining contrast dye safely out of the body.

question: Ten days after delivery, a new mother reports sudden pain, swelling, and redness in her left calf. What condition should you suspect?

options.A: Deep vein thrombosis
options.B: Physiological muscle cramps
options.C: Normal postpartum fatigue
options.D: Inadequate fluid intake

explanation: You've got this! Pain, swelling, and redness in just one leg are classic signs of a blood clot (DVT), which new moms are at higher risk of developing.

question: You notice a family member pressuring a heavily sedated patient to sign a document. What is your best first step as an advocate?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately from the ward
options.B: Ignore it because family financial matters are none of your business
options.C: Intervene to stop the activity and notify the nurse-in-charge or security
options.D: Help the family member hold the pen to finish quickly

explanation: Spot on! Protecting vulnerable, incapacitated patients from exploitation is a core part of your duty as a nurse.

question: Why do nurse-midwives treat every pregnancy as a condition that needs careful monitoring?

options.A: Because it is an inherently pathological state that always causes injury
options.B: Because traditional birth attendants cannot manage normal deliveries
options.C: Because government regulations mandate strict hospital confinement
options.D: Because normal physiological processes can carry unpredictable risks

explanation: Even when a mum is glowing and healthy, things can change quickly. Staying watchful helps us catch any sudden surprises early!

question: A patient is worried that eating fats will only make them gain weight. How can you best explain the good side of fats?

options.A: Fats replace water in cells during dehydration
options.B: Fats are the only nutrient that can build muscle tissue
options.C: Fats protect vital organs and help absorb certain vitamins
options.D: Fats prevent the breakdown of proteins into glucose

explanation: Well done! Dietary fats aren't just about storage; they insulate our organs and are essential for absorbing key vitamins like A, D, E, and K.

question: Why are anti-diarrhea drugs sometimes avoided when a patient has an infection causing their diarrhea?

options.A: Diarrhea helps the kidneys filter extra salt from the blood
options.B: Antibiotics are the only approved treatment for any diarrhea
options.C: These medications always cause permanent bowel paralysis instantly
options.D: Stopping stool too fast can trap harmful bacteria inside the body

explanation: Makes sense, right? Diarrhea is actually the body's way of flushing out bad germs. Shutting it down too quickly can trap those toxins inside.

question: A charge nurse creates the weekly duty roster and assigns patient loads for the morning shift. What type of plan is this?

options.A: Strategic plan
options.B: Visionary plan
options.C: Operational plan
options.D: Tactical plan

explanation: Duty rosters and daily patient assignments are classic examples of short-term operational planning at the unit level. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is the main goal of program implementation in community health?

options.A: Putting planned health interventions into actual practice
options.B: Gathering baseline data before designing an intervention
options.C: Writing the initial budget proposal for a health project
options.D: Assessing the long-term impact of a finished program

explanation: Implementation is all about action! It means taking the written plan and making it happen out there in the community where people need care.

question: Why should a nurse place a convulsing patient in the side-lying recovery position?

options.A: To completely stop the rhythmic shaking of the lower limbs
options.B: To prevent the patient from rolling off the examination bed
options.C: To allow saliva and vomit to drain out and prevent choking
options.D: To make it easier to administer intravenous medications in the arm

explanation: Brilliant! The side-lying position lets saliva or vomit drain safely out of the mouth so the airway stays clear.

question: Which two hormones play the biggest role in helping uterine fibroids grow?

options.A: FSH and LH
options.B: Insulin and glucagon
options.C: Thyroxine and calcitonin
options.D: Estrogen and progesterone

explanation: Estrogen and progesterone fuel the growth of these muscle cells. That is why fibroids are so closely tied to a woman's reproductive years!

question: What key details must be included when writing a family planning referral note?

options.A: A detailed financial breakdown of the hospital delivery bill
options.B: The baby's exact birth weight recorded in ounces and pounds
options.C: Relevant obstetric history and the specific reason for referral
options.D: The nurse's personal home address and phone contact details

explanation: The receiving clinic needs a clear picture of the mother's health history and why she was sent so they can give her the best care.

question: What should you tell a patient who has a normal routine EEG result, but a clear history of seizures?

options.A: The patient's seizures have spontaneously resolved without medical intervention
options.B: A normal EEG does not rule out epilepsy because abnormal waves may not occur during a short test
options.C: The testing equipment was likely calibrated incorrectly during the procedure
options.D: Further neurological evaluation is unnecessary once a normal EEG is recorded

explanation: Routine EEGs only record a short snapshot in time. Many people with true epilepsy have completely normal EEGs between their seizure episodes!

question: Why does exclusive breastfeeding often delay the return of normal menstrual periods?

options.A: The placenta continues to secrete high amounts of progesterone postpartum
options.B: High prolactin levels suppress the release of GnRH from the hypothalamus
options.C: Estrogen levels remain permanently depleted while nursing an infant
options.D: The maternal ovaries completely shut down and atrophy after delivery

explanation: Frequent suckling keeps prolactin levels high, which suppresses the release of hypothalamic releasing hormones that stimulate ovulation. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h5)

question: Which of these is a key part of doing a full, holistic nursing assessment?

options.A: Exploring the patient's home support systems and cultural beliefs
options.B: Avoiding questions about mental health to prevent upsetting them
options.C: Rushing the patient to finish answering interview questions quickly
options.D: Focusing exclusively on laboratory values and bedside monitors

explanation: Awesome! Holistic assessments intentionally gather data on social, cultural, and emotional factors right alongside physical signs.

question: In clinical nursing, how do we truly know how much pain a patient is in?

options.A: Pain only exists if visible tissue damage is present.
options.B: Pain is whatever the experiencing patient says it is.
options.C: Pain is a psychological illusion created by anxiety.
options.D: Pain can be accurately measured solely by high blood pressure.

explanation: Remember this golden rule of nursing: pain is subjective. If the patient says it hurts, it hurts! Always trust and validate your patient's report.

question: What protective gear is a must when handling strong, concentrated chemical disinfectants?

options.A: Sterile surgical gown and shoe covers
options.B: Heavy-duty utility gloves and eye protection
options.C: Clean non-sterile examination gloves
options.D: A standard paper surgical facemask only

explanation: Concentrated disinfectants can sting your skin and damage your eyes. Always wear heavy utility gloves and eye protection!

question: Which socio-cultural factor most commonly discourages men from seeking early healthcare?

options.A: Lack of available male doctors
options.B: Strict government hospital regulations
options.C: Fear of paying high transport costs
options.D: Viewing health-seeking behavior as a sign of weakness

explanation: Traditional definitions of masculinity often make men hide illness or delay seeking help to appear strong. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h2)

question: What happens to a patient's lung if air or fluid gets inside the pleural space?

options.A: The lung remains completely unaffected by the trapped air
options.B: The lung expands rapidly due to increased volume
options.C: The lung fills entirely with blood instead of air
options.D: The lung collapses because negative pressure is lost

explanation: Spot on! When air or fluid enters where it shouldn't, it breaks that delicate vacuum, causing the lung to pull away and collapse.

question: A patient suddenly feels a strong need to pee and leaks a little before reaching the toilet. What is this called?

options.A: Urinary incontinence
options.B: Hematuria
options.C: Renal failure
options.D: Urinary retention

explanation: Incontinence simply means losing control of urine flow. You will see this a lot in clinical rotations!

question: Why must a nurse wear PPE when performing last offices?

options.A: To protect against exposure to infectious body fluids
options.B: To comply with fire safety rules in the hospital
options.C: To prevent the family from recognizing the nurse later
options.D: To keep the nurse's uniform from getting wrinkled

explanation: Pathogens can still be present in bodily fluids after death, making standard precautions and PPE essential for staff safety. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h3)

question: Why are throw rugs considered a major environmental hazard for older adults?

options.A: They make the underlying floor extremely cold
options.B: They absorb too much moisture from the air
options.C: Their edges easily curl up and catch footwear
options.D: They prevent proper cleaning of the floor

explanation: Unsecured rug edges create a sudden lip or barrier that easily catches toes or cane tips, causing trips. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T5#GNS324_U6_T5_h3)

question: Why must nurses apply lubricating eye drops to an unconscious patient who cannot close their eyelids?

options.A: To test the corneal blink reflex every hour
options.B: To prevent corneal drying, ulceration, and infection
options.C: To decrease pressure inside the eyeball
options.D: To stimulate the optic nerve and improve brain activity

explanation: Spot on! Without natural blinking, the eye surface dries out quickly, so artificial tears protect the eyes from painful ulcers.

question: Why is it so important to set clear, specific objectives during the planning stage?

options.A: It guides what activities to do and helps measure future success
options.B: It replaces the need to collect baseline data
options.C: It guarantees that no unexpected problems will ever occur
options.D: It ensures that nurses never have to work in rural areas

explanation: Clear objectives act like a map. They show you your daily steps and let you check later whether you actually reached your destination.

question: Who should you talk to first when introducing a new health program to a traditional community?

options.A: Newly graduated nursing students from the city
options.B: Commercial transport drivers in the motor park
options.C: International donor agencies and foreign embassies
options.D: Community leaders and traditional rulers

explanation: You got it! Respecting elders and local leaders opens the door for the community to trust and accept your health program.

question: How do vision changes in macular degeneration (AMD) differ from cataracts?

options.A: AMD affects side vision first, while cataracts ruin night vision.
options.B: AMD causes sudden total blindness overnight, while cataracts take years.
options.C: AMD affects central vision, while cataracts cause overall blurriness and glare.
options.D: AMD causes intense eye pain, whereas cataracts are painless.

explanation: Macular degeneration targets your sharp central focus (like when reading), leaving side vision alone. Cataracts, on the other hand, just make everything look foggy and hazy.

question: Which electrolyte imbalance is common in advanced bone tumors due to rapid bone breakdown?

options.A: Hypoglycemia
options.B: Hyponatremia
options.C: Hypercalcemia
options.D: Hypokalemia

explanation: When tumors break down bone fast, lots of calcium floods into the bloodstream, leading to hypercalcemia. You've got this down!

question: How does community mobilisation change the way local people take part in health programs?

options.A: It makes villagers responsible for hiring and firing doctors
options.B: It forces community members to fund all local clinic budgets
options.C: It turns passive recipients into active partners in health
options.D: It replaces the need for professional nurses in rural areas

explanation: You got it! Instead of just waiting for health workers to tell them what to do, mobilisation gets community members involved as active partners in their own wellbeing.

question: Why do we sometimes treat a dry, hacking cough with medicine, even though coughing is a natural body defense?

options.A: It prevents oxygen from reaching the brain tissues.
options.B: It stops the heart from beating too fast during sleep.
options.C: It always indicates a permanent lung collapse.
options.D: It causes tiredness and chest pain without bringing up any phlegm.

explanation: A dry cough doesn't help clear anything out—it just leaves your patient exhausted and sore. Treating it helps them get some much-needed rest!

question: Where is the cell body of a preganglionic neuron located?

options.A: Target effector organ
options.B: Skeletal muscle fiber
options.C: Peripheral autonomic ganglion
options.D: Brain or spinal cord

explanation: Preganglionic neurons always originate inside the central nervous system, which includes the brain and spinal cord. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T29#GNS211_U3_T29_h3)

question: A patient comes in complaining of severe tiredness, unexpected weight gain, and feeling cold all the time. Which hormone issue is likely going on?

options.A: Cushing's syndrome
options.B: Hypothyroidism
options.C: Diabetes mellitus
options.D: Hyperthyroidism

explanation: When the thyroid is underactive (hypothyroidism), the whole body's engine slows down, leading to fatigue, sluggishness, and cold intolerance. Great clinical spot!

question: When should a nurse refer a patient for genetic counseling regarding cancer?

options.A: The patient has a strong family history suggesting an inherited gene mutation.
options.B: The patient needs immediate chemotherapy for an active lung tumor.
options.C: The patient wants to quit smoking and needs nicotine replacement therapy.
options.D: The patient requires physical therapy to recover from radiation fatigue.

explanation: If a family history points to inherited genes, genetic counseling helps patients understand their risks and plan ahead.

question: What crucial step must you never forget before pulling out an indwelling catheter?

options.A: Completely deflate the balloon by withdrawing all the sterile water with a syringe
options.B: Apply heat packs to the patient's lower abdomen
options.C: Clamp the catheter for 24 hours to exercise the bladder
options.D: Disconnect the drainage bag and flush the tube with antiseptic solution

explanation: Never skip this! Pulling out a catheter while the balloon is still full will cause severe, painful injury to the patient.

question: What usually happens to red bone marrow in long bones as a person grows older?

options.A: It transforms into active cartilage tissue.
options.B: It turns into yellow bone marrow for fat storage.
options.C: It dissolves completely leaving empty hollow spaces.
options.D: It hardens directly into compact cortical bone.

explanation: As we age, our bodies don't need quite as much active red marrow making blood cells all the time. Much of it converts into yellow marrow, which mainly stores fat (though it can switch back to red if the body urgently needs it!).

question: What is the job of intrinsic activity when a drug acts in the body?

options.A: It measures the weight of the active pharmaceutical ingredient.
options.B: It prevents the drug from entering the bloodstream.
options.C: It triggers a biological response after the drug binds.
options.D: It determines how fast the kidneys clear the medicine.

explanation: Once the drug locks onto its receptor, intrinsic activity is the spark that actually makes the cell change its behavior. Great job learning the basics!

question: What is a major benefit of keeping synovial fluid moving inside a joint?

options.A: It cools down the body when a fever is present.
options.B: It dissolves small blood clots in the bloodstream.
options.C: It permanently locks the joint in a straight position.
options.D: It nourishes the cartilage inside the joint capsule.

explanation: Cartilage doesn't have its own blood supply, so it depends entirely on movement to swish that nourishing synovial fluid around!

question: What major global health crisis drove the rapid development of early mechanical ventilation?

options.A: The polio epidemics of the mid-20th century
options.B: The 1918 influenza pandemic across Europe
options.C: Major outbreaks of cholera in crowded cities
options.D: The rapid rise of severe traumatic road accidents

explanation: The polio epidemics caused widespread respiratory paralysis, forcing hospitals to find mechanical ways to help patients breathe. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h2)

question: In occupational health, what is the FIRST and best line of defense against workplace air hazards?

options.A: Putting up exhaust fans in the work area
options.B: Giving workers certified face masks or respirators
options.C: Rotating shifts so workers spend less time near the hazard
options.D: Completely removing or replacing the dangerous material

explanation: Elimination and substitution are top priorities in safety. If you get rid of the hazard entirely, nobody has to rely on masks or fans to stay safe!

question: What is the primary goal of a research critique?

options.A: To rewrite the entire study for the original authors
options.B: To prove that published research is always correct
options.C: To find minor spelling and formatting errors in a paper
options.D: To evaluate if study findings are trustworthy and useful

explanation: A critique looks closely at a study to judge its overall quality and clinical value rather than focusing on trivial errors. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h1)

question: How can a nurse researcher best cut down on sampling bias?

options.A: Keep the sample size as small as possible to save time
options.B: Use random selection methods and clear inclusion criteria
options.C: Select only friends and family members who agree to participate
options.D: Ignore patients who do not fit the desired research outcome

explanation: You got it! Randomization and clear rules about who can join keep things fair and help your sample truly represent the wider population.

question: What is the most dangerous situation where a barium enema must NEVER be done?

options.A: Well-controlled high blood pressure
options.B: Suspected or known tear (perforation) in the gut
options.C: Mild internal piles without bleeding
options.D: A history of mild, ongoing constipation

explanation: If barium leaks out through a hole in the bowel, it causes severe and dangerous inflammation inside the abdomen. Safety first!

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical feature of untreated or severe endometritis?

options.A: Normal spontaneous resolution without any treatment
options.B: Spread of infection into the bloodstream
options.C: Scarring of the inner uterine cavity
options.D: Formation of pus pockets in the pelvis

explanation: Endometritis is serious and won't just go away on its own. Leaving it untreated can lead to nasty complications like abscesses or blood infections.

question: Which clinical findings form the classic triad of an opioid overdose?

options.A: CNS depression, pinpoint pupils, and respiratory depression
options.B: Dry skin, confusion, and elevated heart rate
options.C: Hypertension, hyperthermia, and dilated pupils
options.D: Diarrhea, excessive sweating, and muscle twitching

explanation: Opioids depress the central nervous system and respiratory centers while typically causing miosis (pinpoint pupils). [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h5)

question: What is 'problem-focused coping' when dealing with a health challenge?

options.A: Blaming other people for causing the physical disability
options.B: Taking direct action to change or fix the stressful situation
options.C: Ignoring the problem completely until it goes away
options.D: Relying entirely on denial and emotional shutdown

explanation: Correct! It's all about practical steps—like learning new skills or modifying the home to handle challenges head-on.

question: Why is hormone therapy often used to treat prostate cancer?

options.A: It replaces the need for surgical removal of the bladder
options.B: Prostate cancer growth is often fueled by male sex hormones
options.C: Hormone drugs permanently cure all forms of kidney tumors
options.D: It stops the kidneys from producing excess red blood cells

explanation: Many prostate cancer cells need testosterone to grow and thrive. By lowering these hormone levels in the body, we can help slow down or shrink the tumor.

question: What heavily shapes how a person expresses grief and mourning?

options.A: The specific brand of hospital bed
options.B: Culture and spiritual beliefs
options.C: The room number in the hospital
options.D: The time of day the patient was admitted

explanation: Spot on! Cultural background and spiritual worldview guide the rituals and social rules for how a community handles loss.

question: Why must a nurse pay attention to non-verbal cues like facial expressions during an assessment?

options.A: Patients may hide their true emotional distress behind polite words
options.B: Non-verbal cues are the only way to measure blood pressure accurately
options.C: Patients expect nurses to read their minds without asking questions
options.D: Hospital regulations require charting body language every hour

explanation: Exactly! People often say they are fine while their body language quietly reveals anxiety, pain, or fear.

question: What is the main surgical option used to treat severe stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: Widening the urethral opening with a stent
options.B: Placing a supportive sling under the urethra
options.C: Implanting an artificial kidney to filter urine
options.D: Removing the lower portion of the bladder

explanation: A surgical sling acts like a little hammock or seatbelt underneath the urethra to keep it from dropping when you move.

question: During a quick check right after birth, which sign tells you the newborn is doing great?

options.A: Meconium present in the amniotic fluid
options.B: A slow and irregular breathing pattern
options.C: Pale skin and limp extremities
options.D: Good muscle tone and crying

explanation: A baby who cries loudly, moves their arms and legs, and has good muscle tone is telling you their brain and lungs are working wonderfully!

question: When two rescuers are doing CPR on a child, what is the compression-to-ventilation ratio?

options.A: 5 compressions to 1 breath
options.B: 30 compressions to 2 breaths
options.C: 100 compressions to 5 breaths
options.D: 15 compressions to 2 breaths

explanation: When you have two people working together on a pediatric patient, you use a 15:2 ratio to get more rescue breaths into the child.

question: Where does fertilization usually happen inside the fallopian tube?

options.A: Infundibulum
options.B: Isthmus
options.C: Ampulla
options.D: Fimbriae

explanation: Brilliant! The ampulla is the wide middle part of the tube where the sperm and egg love to meet.

question: What symptom turns pre-eclampsia into full-blown eclampsia?

options.A: Total cessation of fetal heart tones
options.B: A sudden drop in body temperature
options.C: The onset of convulsive seizures
options.D: Severe localized pain in the lower back

explanation: Spot on! Pre-eclampsia has high blood pressure and protein in the urine, but once seizures start, it is classified as eclampsia.

question: What do you call bending the foot so the toes point upward toward the shin?

options.A: Abduction
options.B: Dorsiflexion
options.C: Plantar flexion
options.D: Pronation

explanation: You got it! Dorsiflexion means pulling the ankle up so the top of the foot moves closer to the leg.

question: Which of these symptoms is a classic danger sign that could mean a pregnant woman is developing pre-eclampsia?

options.A: Mild swelling of the fingers in the morning
options.B: Occasional lower back pain
options.C: Severe headache and blurred vision
options.D: Increased appetite for sweet foods

explanation: Severe headaches and changes in vision are big red flags for dangerously high blood pressure (pre-eclampsia). Always take this seriously!

question: Even though prolactin is high during pregnancy, why doesn't heavy milk production start right away?

options.A: Oxytocin suppresses milk synthesis until the baby is born
options.B: High levels of estrogen and progesterone block prolactin action
options.C: The alveoli are not yet fully formed until labor begins
options.D: The placenta actively destroys prolactin in the maternal blood

explanation: During pregnancy, the placenta keeps high levels of estrogen and progesterone around, which acts like a block on full milk production. Once the baby and placenta are delivered, that block lifts!

question: What is the main reason nurses use the Barthel Index assessment tool?

options.A: To diagnose the primary neurological cause of paralysis
options.B: To measure a patient's independence in activities of daily living
options.C: To test the patient's long-term memory capacity
options.D: To calculate the exact dosage of pain medication needed

explanation: The Barthel Index is simply a helpful scoring guide to see how well a patient can handle basic tasks like eating, washing, and moving around.

question: What is the first step a nurse should take to control severe external bleeding on an arm?

options.A: Apply direct, firm pressure to the wound
options.B: Administer a large dose of intravenous fluids
options.C: Apply a tight tourniquet immediately above the elbow
options.D: Elevate the injured arm above the heart level

explanation: Direct pressure is always the initial and most effective method for controlling external hemorrhage before resorting to a tourniquet. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h5)

question: What is your immediate nursing action if you notice an umbilical cord prolapse during labor?

options.A: administering an intramuscular dose of oxytocin to speed up delivery
options.B: elevating the presenting fetal part off the cord with a gloved hand
options.C: encouraging the mother to push with maximum effort during contractions
options.D: preparing the patient for immediate induction using prostaglandins

explanation: You got it! You must instantly relieve pressure off the cord with your hand to keep oxygen flowing to the baby until emergency help arrives.

question: How many hours of fasting are normally needed before a fasting blood sugar test?

options.A: 2 to 4 hours
options.B: 18 to 24 hours
options.C: 8 to 12 hours
options.D: Exactly 30 minutes

explanation: An 8 to 12 hour fast (usually overnight) gives the body enough time to clear out food from the last meal so we get a true baseline reading.

question: A clinic administrator is buying medications following the National Drug Policy. What should guide this choice?

options.A: Purchasing large quantities of single-use antibiotics regardless of disease patterns
options.B: Focusing on safety, efficacy, affordability, and availability of essential medicines
options.C: Stocking only medications that are heavily advertised on television and radio
options.D: Buying the most expensive imported brands to guarantee maximum patient prestige

explanation: When stocking a clinic, we always look for drugs that are safe, work well, patients can afford, and are actually available when needed!

question: Your patient is recovering from joint surgery. What is the best nursing action to help them heal?

options.A: Encourage early, supervised movement within safe physical limits
options.B: Keep the patient strictly confined to bed for at least two weeks
options.C: Discourage any physical therapy to avoid all post-operative pain
options.D: Administer heavy sedatives to keep the patient entirely immobile

explanation: Getting moving early (safely, of course!) prevents stiffness, improves blood flow, and speeds up recovery.

question: Which sign during a thoracocentesis might indicate a vasovagal reaction?

options.A: Dizziness, sweating, and a sudden drop in heart rate
options.B: A rapid spike in blood pressure and excessive talking
options.C: Sudden redness and warmth spreading over the face
options.D: An intense urge to cough continuously for ten minutes

explanation: Pain, anxiety, or fluid shifts can trigger a vasovagal response, causing low heart rate, low blood pressure, and dizziness. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h5)

question: Why must a nurse check a female patient's surgical history before placing an IV in her arm?

options.A: To confirm she is not currently allergic to standard soap.
options.B: To avoid placing an IV on the same side as a prior mastectomy.
options.C: To make sure she has never received a blood transfusion before.
options.D: To ensure her blood pressure can be measured safely on that arm.

explanation: Lymph node removal during a mastectomy impairs lymphatic drainage, making that arm vulnerable to swelling and severe infection if punctured. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of using screening tools like CAGE or ASSIST in nursing?

options.A: To identify substance use problems early before they become severe
options.B: To gather legal evidence for immediate arrest by police officers
options.C: To test the chemical purity of substances seized on the street
options.D: To calculate the exact financial cost of a patient's drug habit

explanation: These quick screening tools help us spot risky habits early so we can step in with support before things get out of hand.

question: Why did military nursing groups become so important during the Crusades?

options.A: To translate ancient Greek philosophy texts
options.B: To provide organized shelter and treat wounded soldiers
options.C: To manufacture advanced gunpowder and tactical weapons
options.D: To govern newly conquered political territories

explanation: During the Crusades, special nursing groups were needed to set up safe resting places and care for fighters and travelers who got hurt.

question: What is the most important ingredient for a community health program to actually work?

options.A: Active community participation
options.B: Building multi-storey hospital complexes
options.C: Complete absence of local traditional healers
options.D: Exclusive funding from foreign donors

explanation: You can have all the funding in the world, but if the local people aren't involved and on board, the program won't last. Community ownership is key!

question: Which patient group requires the greatest caution when taking anticholinergic medications?

options.A: Older adult patients
options.B: Young children with fevers
options.C: Pregnant women in their first trimester
options.D: Athletes with muscle sprains

explanation: Older adults are much more sensitive to side effects like confusion, constipation, and urinary retention, increasing complication risks. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T6#GNS223_U5_T6_h6)

question: What happens when antibodies in a patient's plasma encounter unfamiliar red blood cell antigens?

options.A: They convert the foreign antigens into safe body proteins
options.B: They absorb the extra antigens to nourish surrounding tissues
options.C: They dissolve the donor red blood cells into liquid plasma
options.D: They bind to the foreign cells and cause agglutination

explanation: Plasma antibodies attack unfamiliar antigens by latching onto them, which makes the red blood cells clump together. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T8#GNS123_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why do nurses love using infrared thermometers on a busy hospital ward?

options.A: It prints out a paper record automatically
options.B: It captures temperature quickly without touching the skin
options.C: It measures core temperature directly from the heart
options.D: It never needs new batteries or calibration

explanation: You'll find these handy on the ward because they let you screen patients fast without needing physical skin contact. Great for keeping things moving!

question: What does the term 'hidden hunger' mean in public health?

options.A: Micronutrient deficiencies from diets lacking essential vitamins and minerals
options.B: Eating too many high-protein foods in a single meal
options.C: Extreme starvation caused by total crop failure
options.D: A condition where people hide their food out of fear of theft

explanation: Exactly right! Hidden hunger happens when someone gets enough belly-filling calories from cheap starchy foods, but misses out on vital vitamins and minerals.

question: A client comes to the clinic saying her partner's condom tore three hours ago. What advice should you give?

options.A: Avoid emergency contraception because it only works after 72 hours
options.B: Wait exactly 48 hours before taking any action to let natural cycles adjust
options.C: Come back next week for a pregnancy test before doing anything
options.D: Take the emergency contraceptive as soon as possible for the highest effectiveness

explanation: When accidents happen like a torn condom, acting fast is key. Taking the pill right away gives the client the highest chance of preventing a pregnancy.

question: Which physical sign do nurses check first to quickly spot possible anaemia?

options.A: Swelling in the upper eyelids
options.B: Yellow color in the eyes
options.C: Pallor of the inner eyelids and nail beds
options.D: Dryness of the outer ears

explanation: Looking at the conjunctiva and nail beds is a quick, classic nursing trick to check if blood color looks healthy and pink!

question: Why is documenting telephone orders from a physician crucial in home care?

options.A: It serves as a receipt for the pharmacy to give discounts to the client
options.B: It allows the nurse to prescribe medications independently without a doctor
options.C: It protects the nurse legally and ensures clear instructions are followed without miscommunication
options.D: It is only done to impress visiting supervisors during an audit

explanation: Documenting who gave the order, when, and the exact details prevents dangerous medication errors and provides a clear audit trail. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is the core philosophy of family-centered care in pediatrics?

options.A: Viewing the family as an essential partner in the child's healthcare
options.B: Focusing exclusively on hospital-based procedures
options.C: Excluding family members from daily medical decisions
options.D: Treating the child without input from the parents

explanation: Family-centered care builds on the strengths of families and honors their central role in the child's life. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h7)

question: Which sign strongly suggests a patient's sting site is developing a bacterial infection days later?

options.A: Spreading erythema, warmth, and purulent discharge at the site days later
options.B: Immediate localized pain and minor itching right after the sting
options.C: Clear fluid blisters that form and heal within twenty-four hours
options.D: A small drop in blood pressure within the first five minutes

explanation: Watch out for spreading redness (erythema), feeling hot to the touch, and pus (purulent discharge)—these are classic signs that bacteria have set in.

question: A patient has a deep pressure ulcer on their heel that is draining a lot of fluid. Which dressing is best to handle it?

options.A: Transparent film
options.B: Dry cotton gauze
options.C: Foam dressing
options.D: Paper tape

explanation: Foam dressings are fantastic at cushioning fragile skin while soaking up moderate-to-heavy drainage. Spot on!

question: How does aseptic technique differ from everyday household cleaning?

options.A: Aseptic technique is only performed by medical doctors
options.B: Aseptic technique aims for the complete absence of disease-producing microbes
options.C: Household cleaning uses stronger bleach solutions than hospitals
options.D: Household cleaning is regulated by strict international health laws

explanation: While cleaning removes visible dirt, aseptic technique specifically targets invisible pathogens to protect patients during vulnerable procedures. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is the main focus of a nurse manager practicing servant leadership?

options.A: Writing policy manuals without clinical input
options.B: Supporting the nursing staff so they can provide great patient care
options.C: Maximizing financial profit for the hospital board
options.D: Enforcing strict rules without listening to staff feedback

explanation: Servant leadership flips the pyramid! Instead of bossing people around, the manager sees their job as removing roadblocks so the frontline nurses can shine.

question: Besides the patient, who else is at high risk and needs emotional support during cancer recovery?

options.A: Pharmaceutical suppliers
options.B: Billing department staff
options.C: Hospital administrators
options.D: Family caregivers

explanation: Don't forget the family! Caregivers pour so much energy into helping others that they often face severe stress and burnout themselves.

question: A head nurse lets staff nurses help make the duty roster and gives them freedom in patient care. Which theory is she using?

options.A: Utilitarianism
options.B: Classical management
options.C: Theory Y
options.D: Theory X

explanation: Theory Y is the optimistic approach! It assumes workers are self-motivated, enjoy taking on responsibilities, and thrive when given professional freedom.

question: Why do many Nigerian women traditionally practice hot water baths or steaming after childbirth?

options.A: To cleanse the womb and aid postpartum recovery
options.B: To lower systemic blood pressure levels
options.C: To increase breast milk sodium concentration
options.D: To prevent the development of gestational diabetes

explanation: Great job thinking about cultural context! Traditional practices like hot water steaming are often used to help the body heal and purify after delivery. Understanding this helps us care for mothers better.

question: Why is keeping a narrow range for vital signs important for a patient?

options.A: It ensures the patient stays awake during the night
options.B: It guarantees that blood pressure never changes
options.C: It prevents vital organs from failing due to extreme stress
options.D: It stops the patient from needing any medication

explanation: Great thinking! Staying within a safe, normal range protects your patient's cells and organs from being overworked by extreme highs and lows.

question: Which type of glaucoma happens suddenly and comes with severe pain because the drainage angle is completely blocked?

options.A: Angle-closure glaucoma
options.B: Secondary pigmentary glaucoma
options.C: Open-angle glaucoma
options.D: Normal-tension glaucoma
